subject: Proposed language: incident escalation, subprocessors, and cross-border data flow
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@finexcorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: privacy_ops@finexcorp.com
Date: 2027-05-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarification needed: incident notification timelines & subprocessors

Marissa,

Thanks for the DPA draft — small set of questions from our security and procurement teams so we can move to legal sign-off. Can you confirm the following items and, if possible, provide proposed clause language we can mark up?

1) Notification windows: does Redwood commit to an initial acknowledgement timeline and a firm window for "confirmed" incidents? Our policy requests a 72-hour detailed notification after confirmation, but we want to understand any operational exceptions.

2) Scope of notice: do you define what constitutes "personal data" for notice triggers? Will there be a materiality threshold (e.g., number of records, risk)?

3) Evidence & cooperation: what level of log/evidence handover can we expect, and within what timeframe? Is there an expectation for full forensic data export or limited exports (redacted/pseudonymized)?

4) Subprocessors & transfers: can you share your current subprocessor list and confirm how you will handle new subprocessors (notification window)? For cross-border processing, do you rely on SCCs, adequacy, or other mechanisms?

If you can send suggested language and any attachments (redlines) we’ll circulate to counsel and privacy. Our counsel (cc'd) may want to propose additional controls or SLA remedies.

Appreciate the quick turn — we are hoping to finalize within this week if possible.

Thanks,
Samir Patel
Head of Security Operations
FinexCorp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@finexcorp.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-09T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification needed: incident notification timelines & subprocessors

Samir — thanks for the clear list. I’ve attached a marked-up DPA excerpt (redwood_incident_clause_markups.docx) with proposed language; summary of the main points below. Please review and flag anything you want tightened.

Summary of proposed clause language (high level):
- Acknowledgement: initial acknowledgement within 24 hours of Redwood becoming aware of an event that may reasonably affect customer data.
- Preliminary notice: for incidents confirmed to meet the DPA definition, Redwood will provide a preliminary notice within 72 hours containing affected systems, data types (high-level), severity, and next steps.
- Detailed follow-up & evidence: for high-severity incidents (material exposure of personal data), Redwood will provide a technical incident report and available evidence within 5 business days where operationally feasible; ongoing evidence cooperation will be provided as needed.
- Subprocessor notifications: Redwood will publish a current subprocessor list and provide at least 10 business days' notice before onboarding subprocessors that process Customer Personal Data; emergency onboarding exceptions require post-notification and documented justification.
- Cross-border transfers: Redwood relies on SCCs where required and will provide its export/transfer mechanisms on request; copies of executed SCCs can be shared under NDA.

We tried to balance speed (acknowledgement + preliminary 72-hour window) with operational realities for evidence collection (5 business days for technical package). Rishi and Neha are looped for legal/security redlines.

Next steps: Rishi/neha — can you review the attached and propose any firm edits? Samir — if those timelines look generally okay, I’ll circulate the redline back to your counsel.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-10T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed language: incident escalation, subprocessors, and cross-border data flow

Marissa — quick legal redlines after a first pass on your markup. High level: we can accept the 24-hour ack + 72-hour preliminary, but recommend the following clarifications to avoid open-ended obligations:

- Evidence scope: change "technical incident report and available evidence" to "relevant logs and metadata reasonably necessary for Customer to assess impact"; reserve full forensic exports for where mutually agreed or required by law.
- Operational carve-outs: add language that timelines are subject to reasonable delays needed for active remediation/investigation and to preserve evidence integrity.
- SLA remedies: avoid open-ended monetary penalties for missed notice windows; propose service credits tied to demonstrable process failures (draft cap: 5% of monthly fees for the affected service).

Also flag: consult with Security on the definition of "high-severity" — we should map to our internal incident classification to make handovers consistent. If acceptable, I'll fold these into the draft and we can send to Finex counsel.

Rishi
Deputy General Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-10T11:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed language: incident escalation, subprocessors, and cross-border data flow

Adding security perspective / minor edits:

- Acknowledgement: 24 hours ok. Preliminary 72-hour notice is acceptable provided we explicitly state that the preliminary notice is "to the extent known at the time".
- Evidence transfer: recommend we commit to a technical package for confirmed high-severity incidents within 5 business days that includes: incident timeline, affected services, indicators of compromise, and relevant logs (redacted where necessary). Full raw logs or backups only where legally required or by mutual written agreement.
- Subprocessors: attach current disclosure matrix (subprocessor_disclosure_matrix.pdf). Recommend we promise publication of changes and a 30-day notice for non-emergency additions that process customer personal data. Emergency subprocessors to be disclosed within 5 business days after onboarding with justification.
- Cross-border: confirm use of SCCs and internal DPIA for any transfer that relies on SCCs. Will provide executed SCCs to customers under NDA.

If everyone agrees I can add a short technical appendix to the DPA that references our incident classification and what "evidence package" contains.

Neha Kapoor
Director, Security & Privacy Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@finexcorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ellison Partners (counsel) <counsel@ellisonpartners.com>, privacy_ops@finexcorp.com
Date: 2027-05-11T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed language: incident escalation, subprocessors, and cross-border data flow

Marissa / team — thanks, that’s helpful. Counsel reviewed Rishi's and Neha's points and we are broadly aligned with the proposed approach. A few items we’d like to confirm before approving the edits:

1) Evidence handover timeline: Finex is comfortable with a 5-business-day technical package for high-severity incidents, but we also need a guaranteed maximum of 5 calendar days for production of the primary evidence package (to avoid business-calendar confusion). Can Redwood confirm 5 calendar days as the upper bound for the technical package?

2) SLA credit: we prefer a defined credit schedule for missed notification obligations (tiered by severity). We can accept a cap, please confirm the 5% cap suggestion from legal.

3) Cross-border transfers: confirm you will provide executed SCCs for EU→US processing and any other required mechanisms; if Redwood requires an NDA to share SCCs, please include that in your response.

Assuming answers to the three items above are satisfactory Finex legal will prepare a clean DPA for signature. Please send a DocuSign link once the final is ready.

Samir
Head of Security Operations, FinexCorp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@finexcorp.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-12T16:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed language: incident escalation, subprocessors, and cross-border data flow

Samir — thanks, and appreciate the quick review from counsel. Final positions from Redwood below; attaching the final marked DPA for signature (DPA_Finex_20270512-markup.docx) and publishing our subprocessor matrix.

Responses:
- Evidence handover: Redwood confirms a 5 calendar day upper bound for delivery of the initial technical package for confirmed high-severity incidents where the data necessary for that package is available to Redwood. As legal noted, timelines may be paused only to preserve evidence integrity during active forensic containment; pauses to be documented and communicated.
- SLA credit: Redwood can accept a capped service credit remedy of up to 5% of monthly fees for the affected service for failures to meet notice obligations that are the result of process failures (not investigation delays). We'll include a short schedule in the DPA.
- Cross-border/SCCs: Redwood will provide executed SCCs under NDA. I’ve included a link to the DocuSign envelope and the drive folder with the SCC template and our export controls.

DocuSign link: https://app.docusign.com/documents/ABC123-finex-dpa
Drive folder (SCCs & matrix): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b-finex-dpa-exchange

Next steps:
1) Counsel to review attached final markup and route for signature.
2) We will provide executed SCCs under NDA and publish any required subprocessor notices.
3) I’ll schedule a short alignment call if you’d like to walk through the technical appendix.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
Attachments: DPA_Finex_20270512-markup.docx
